title: US strikes Qeshm on the eve of the vote, and a deadly night for Ukraine
summary: Limited US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island as Vance talks up a deal, one of the deadliest Russian strikes of the war at an aid centre in Komyshuvakha, a huge overnight barrage on Ukraine's grid and a Kharkiv hospital, Ukraine's strike on the Yaroslavl refinery, and the Theodore Roosevelt moving into the South China Sea.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so use us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Tuesday, November third. Election day in the US. And the last twenty-four hours have been heavy, both in the Gulf and in Ukraine.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's start in the Gulf, because there's a genuine contradiction to unpack. On Monday, the United States struck Iran's Qeshm Island, right in the Strait of Hormuz.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And at almost the same moment, Vice President Vance was saying he feels good about a deal.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Exactly. So, the strikes first. US officials told CNN, NBC and ABC these were limited, defensive strikes. They say Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired at an American aircraft, and the strike was aimed at the launcher. And they stressed this was not a return to major combat.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Iranian state media reported explosions on the island. Iran's deputy foreign minister said Tehran reserves the right to defend itself. And Central Command didn't comment.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: There's also a Wall Street Journal report that this was the latest in a series of limited US strikes in recent weeks, and that the earlier ones weren't publicised.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now the diplomacy. Vance told CNN that he and the president feel good about a negotiated settlement, and that Washington hasn't set a deadline. Remember yesterday we mentioned his letter to Iran's security chief.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: But an Iranian official told Reuters the two sides are still far apart. Iran's position is that its conditions have to be met first, then Hormuz reopens, and only after that can nuclear talks start.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Qatari mediators were heading back to Tehran with a draft deal. And markets clearly liked the tone. Oil fell more than six percent on Monday.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So the picture is pressure and talks at the same time. And all of it on the eve of an election that US officials had reportedly flagged as a decision point.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Let's turn to Ukraine. And I'll be honest, this is a hard one.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Yeah. On Monday, Russian guided bombs hit a school in the village of Komyshuvakha, in Zaporizhzhia region. The school was being used as a humanitarian aid centre.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: At least nine guided bombs, according to Ukrainian reporting. President Zelensky says thirty-three people were killed, with more possibly still under the rubble. Two rescue workers and four police officers are among the dead.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The region has declared three days of mourning. The UN's human rights monitoring mission said the attack appeared to violate fundamental principles of international humanitarian law. Russia's defence ministry says it was targeting Ukrainian military units around the village.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And then, overnight into today, a massive barrage. Zelensky says Russia launched two hundred and eighty-nine drones, seventeen ballistic missiles and fifty-nine cruise missiles.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The main target was energy. Power plants and substations in several regions, with emergency blackouts now in place. But one strike hit a hospital in Kharkiv.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Prosecutors say seventy-three people were injured there. Patients, medical staff and people living nearby. Two hundred and twenty-six patients had to be moved to other hospitals.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And Ukraine kept up its own long-range campaign. Overnight, drones hit the Slavneft refinery in Yaroslavl, northeast of Moscow. It's Russia's fifth-largest refinery. The governor confirmed the hit and said two workers were hurt.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Footage showed at least seven fires. Russia's defence ministry claims it shot down eight hundred and fifty-six Ukrainian drones overnight, over half of them aimed at the Moscow area. And in occupied Crimea, Russian-installed officials say attacks on the power grid caused blackouts in at least five cities.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So if you've been following this week, that's the Novokuybyshevsk, Ufa and Kstovo refineries, a Samara oil hub, and now Yaroslavl. In about five days.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: While Russia, in turn, hits Ukraine's grid on a massive scale. It's very much an energy war in both directions heading into winter.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the ground, Ukraine's General Staff reported two hundred and six clashes on Monday. The busiest front was Kostiantynivka, with twenty-one Russian attacks, and thirteen more near Pokrovsk.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Okay, quick lap of the other fronts. Yemen. Saudi Arabia's coalition says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired toward the south of the kingdom. Civil defence sent alerts to Khamis Mushait, Abha, Taif and Najran before sounding the all-clear.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And in Gaza, the civil defence agency says Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed five people on Monday, including one in a strike on a vehicle in Gaza City. The Israeli military says it targeted militants.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now, the ships. And there's actually movement this time. The new USNI fleet tracker puts the carrier Theodore Roosevelt in the South China Sea. It finished exercise Keen Sword with Japan and is moving west.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Which fits the earlier report from Fox News, citing US officials, that the Roosevelt group is headed for the Middle East. If it keeps going, the route is through the Strait of Malacca and into the Indian Ocean.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The George Washington and the George H. W. Bush are still reported in the Arabian Sea. And the Makin Island amphibious group was last confirmed in Yokosuka on October twenty-sixth. Its current position isn't public, so we've marked it as low confidence on the map.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch. The US election results, and whether the Qeshm strikes stay limited or become something bigger. Whether Qatar's draft deal gets anywhere in Tehran. And whether the Roosevelt turns up in the Indian Ocean in the next tracker.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And in Ukraine, how the power grid holds up after last night, and the funerals in Komyshuvakha this week.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
